correctness.rationale: Unique first-column seed recurrence with v0=v(n+1)=0 is equivalent to all grid equations. Exact finite matrices have rank sequences (1,1,0), (2,1,2,0), (3,3,1,3,3,0), (4,4,4,4,0); Fp=0 and invertible adjacent transition establish all residue kernels. On admitted seed kernels v_p=0, reflection yields t copies and proves scaling for all lengths. Exhaustive base lists give nonzero word multiplicities and deduplicated complete-rank support spectra, with generalized weights their minima. Prime lists explicitly exclude zero rows and columns. Independent direct parity enumeration of 74,954 small arrays plus recurrence checks for 288 pairs confirm the base and sampled consequences; the infinite proof does not depend on finite extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Full 2026 Klostermeyer manuscript and closely related 2005 article attribute the binary Fibonacci recursion, seed space, nullity count and zero-column reflection to prior work. Those premises are explicitly credited. The reviewed original claim instead gives six complete all-length Hamming enumerators, identifies first width with two nonzero weights, and counts every rank/support type for the infinite four-row strip family. Nullity 2^d does not imply a weight spectrum, and square nullity/prime status does not imply the full subcode-support spectrum. Direct equivalence, broader-coverage, database and implication searches identified no known stronger or equivalent full invariant, although the inaccessible full 2002 paper and alternative terminology present material residual-priority risks.

value.rationale: The code-size/solvability data of classical parity-grid papers leave the exact number of feasible subsets of a prescribed size undetermined. A full spectrum and every higher-support subcode count are natural invariants for error-detecting binary codes and combinatorial Lights Out/closed-parity configurations. Width four is the first nontrivial low-width transition from constant to two nonzero weights, and the reflection argument extends a complete 4-row rank-support table to infinitely many lengths. This is an exact nonroutine structural classification; the known recurrence and isolated small-square primeness are not separately counted as discoveries.
